record.paper_title: Solutions to open problems in Neeb's recent survey on infinite-dimensional Lie groups
record.original_question: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the subgroup of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms of M that fix p and whose tangent map at p has positive determinant. Let G_f^n(R)_0 be the group of formal diffeomorphisms of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant. After choosing a local chart phi around p with phi(p)=0, is every element of G_f^n(R)_0 realized as the Taylor series at 0 of phi composed with gamma composed with phi^{-1}, for some gamma in Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G_f^n(R)_0 surjective?

evidence.quote: Moreover, we prove a result by the author announced in [21], which answers a question posed in an earlier, unpublished version of the survey.

Let M be σ-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, and Diff c (M) be the Lie group of smooth diffeomorphisms γ : M → M which are compactly supported in the sense that the closure of {x ∈ M : γ(x) 6= x} is compact

Given p ∈ M, let Diff c (M)p be its stabilizer, and Diff c (M)p,0 be the subgroup of all γ ∈ Diff c (M)p such that det Tp (γ) > 0, where Tp (γ) : Tp M →Tp M is the tangent map. Let Gf n (R) ⊆ R[[x1 , . . . , xn ]] be the group of all formal diffeomorphisms of Rn , and Gf n (R)0 be the subgroup of all formal diffeomorphisms whose linear part has positive determinant

Borel’s Theorem for Diffeomorphisms. Let a finite-dimensional smooth manifold M of dimension n be given, p ∈ M and φ be a local chart around p such that φ(p) = 0. For each γ ∈ Diff c (M), let Tp∞ (γ) denote the Taylor series of φ ◦ γ ◦ φ−1 around 0. Then Tp∞ : Diff c (M)p,0 → Gf n (R)0 is a surjective homomorphism of Lie groups.
In this case, the surjectivity of Tp∞ : Diff c (Rn )p,0 → Gf n (R)0 has been established in Lemma 4.2. The Chain Rule for Taylor Polynomials entails that Tp∞ is a homomorphism of groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a $\sigma$-compact smooth manifold of finite dimension $n>0$. Let $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)$ denote the group of smooth diffeomorphisms $\gamma:M\to M$ that are compactly supported, in the sense that the closure of $\{x\in M:\gamma(x)\neq x\}$ is compact. Fix a point $p\in M$, and let $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_p$ be the stabilizer of $p$ in $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)$. Define
\[
\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}=\{\gamma\in\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_p:\det T_p(\gamma)>0\},
\]
where $T_p(\gamma):T_pM\to T_pM$ is the tangent map at $p$.

Let $G_f^n(\mathbb{R})\subseteq \mathbb{R}[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]^n$ denote the group of formal diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (formal power series with zero constant term and invertible linear part, under composition), and let $G_f^n(\mathbb{R})_0$ denote the subgroup consisting of those formal diffeomorphisms whose linear part has positive determinant.

Choose a smooth chart $\varphi$ around $p$ with $\varphi(p)=0$. For $\gamma\in\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}$, let $T_p^\infty(\gamma)\in G_f^n(\mathbb{R})_0$ denote the Taylor series at $0$ of $\varphi\circ\gamma\circ\varphi^{-1}$.

Determine whether the group homomorphism
\[
T_p^\infty:\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}\longrightarrow G_f^n(\mathbb{R})_0
\]
is surjective; equivalently, whether every formal diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with positive-determinant linear part arises as the Taylor expansion at $p$ (in the chart $\varphi$) of some compactly supported smooth diffeomorphism of $M$ fixing $p$ with positive-determinant tangent map at $p$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Taylor-series homomorphism is shown to be surjective ("Borel's Theorem for Diffeomorphisms"), so the question is solved affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Solutions to open problems in Neeb's survey on infinite-dimensional Lie groups
status_evidence.snippet: Borel's Theorem for Diffeomorphisms. ... Then T_p^\infty : Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G_f^n(R)_0 is a surjective homomorphism of Lie groups.
status_evidence.claim: The surjectivity of the Taylor-series homomorphism is established.
